reference-snapshots.justification: .repos contains tracked upstream source snapshots, not installed workspaces. The reference sync copies complete trees after stripping .git, including historical manifests and lockfiles. AGENTS.md prohibits edits/imports; workspace globs, root lock importers and production staging do not include .repos. Dependency graph discovery still sees these manifests. Excluding version updates does not clear security alerts. Revalidate if references become imported, built or shipped.

proposedDismissal.comment: Tracked .repos snapshots are read-only upstream references. They are outside root workspaces, imports and DMG/CLI staging; their manifests are not installed or built. Retained as source reference, not product dependencies. Re-review if workspace/import/build scope changes.

zod3-tooling.justification: Zod 3.25.76 is reached through Expo CLI and Vercel config tooling, not the audited server/desktop/web production closure. Those consumers use Zod 3 APIs; forcing Zod 4 is not a compatible fix. Registry metadata showed no patched Zod 3 release. Keep the alert open and recheck compatible upstream fixes every run. Human risk acceptance has not been granted.

deepmerge-tooling.justification: deepmerge 4.3.1 is reached through build/development tools and absent the audited server/desktop/web production closure. The advisory suggests 4.3.2, but that version was not published at review. Keep exposure open, recheck publication every run and review build input trust. Human risk acceptance has not been granted.

xml-parser-fix.justification: Web extendedDocumentPreview uses XMLParser for ODS/EPUB, reached from the binary preview worker. It does not enable the advisory stopNodes option; locked defaults are empty. Upgrade the affected 5.7.3 to published age-qualified 5.12.0 nonetheless. Local audit and artifact checks must confirm the effective version; main remains affected until merge and fresh verification.

localRemediation.validation: Frozen install passes; fresh all-severity audit no longer reports GHSA-474x-hrwr-fgx4. Web production closure resolves fast-xml-parser 5.12.0 with no missing edges.
localRemediation.mainVerification: pending human merge and fresh main audit/analysis

node-forge-fix.justification: node-forge 1.4.1 is outside the audited server/desktop/web production closure, reached by signing/build tools. Update the frozen lock and conditional override to published age-qualified 1.4.3, addressing all four current advisories. No lifecycle grant change. Keep pending until validation and main merge.

localRemediation.validation: Frozen install passes; fresh all-severity audit no longer reports any of the four node-forge advisories. Server/desktop/web production closures contain no node-forge.
localRemediation.mainVerification: pending human merge and fresh main audit/analysis

polynomial-regex.justification: Reported runtime-source regular expressions include parsers, trailing-run normalizers and Git/SSH/provider helpers. Upstream provenance is verified, but attacker input bounds and final reachability are not proved for every sink. No rule-wide false-positive or inherited-code waiver. Triage bounded groups and retain each alert identity.

runtime-redos.justification: The workflow recognizer has nested repetition over whitespace/comments; the scoped-package recognizer repeats a slash-containing character class. Reported expressions occur in upstream runtime source. Replace with linear recognition preserving behavior and add focused adversarial regression proof before claiming fixed.

tooling-redos.justification: Eval shell-grading parser processes provider output. Tooling placement does not prove trusted input or bounded work; assess input bounds and replace hazardous recognition rather than dismissing as a test.

constant-script-input.justification: Reported bootstrap script substitutions are fixed module-owned CSS/message/key constants; GuestInput editing commands are selected from selectAll/undo/redo, and the mobile overflow message is fixed. Source supports false positives at these serialization boundaries, not a general HTML safety claim. Retain JSON serialization and inspect changed flows on re-review.

proposedDismissal.comment: At the reported serialization boundary the interpolated value is a fixed module constant or an allowlisted editing command; no attacker-owned executable text reaches that substitution. Preserve the existing JSON/script boundary.

test-shell.justification: Test subprocesses execute reviewed fixture shells under the test runner. The fork installer test passes its temporary prefix as positional argv, not shell source. Trusted checkout/process.execPath and fixture-controlled environment are the test boundary; untrusted dependency/PR content must not be interpolated into executable shell text. This is a test disposition, not an install.sh production approval.

proposedDismissal.comment: This subprocess belongs to a fixture test. Shell source is reviewed fixture code; temporary paths/prefixes are passed as positional argv under the trusted test runner, not interpolated attacker shell input.

test-transformations.justification: Reported sanitization/tag-filter/URL operations are assertions or extraction of known fixture scripts for VM tests, not authorization or safe rendering of attacker HTML. Preserve test assertions; do not rewrite them merely to hide a scan result.

proposedDismissal.comment: The reported transformation is a test assertion or known fixture-script extraction, not a production sanitization or URL authorization boundary.

display-text.justification: Reported tag removal feeds plain prompt text, React/native text children or an emptiness decision. These consumers do not interpret the returned string as sanitized HTML. The release-notes update path is excluded from this group and remains separately unresolved.

proposedDismissal.comment: The result is plain text or an emptiness check, not HTML passed to an executable HTML sink; the reported replacement is not used as a security sanitizer.

release-notes-owner.justification: Release-notes conversion needs its final sink and release/update boundary reviewed with the signing/OTA owner. This task does not edit updater or installer code. Upstream origin does not waive the finding.

markdown-backslash.justification: generatedImageMarkdown explicitly percent-encodes backslashes before embedding a Markdown destination, contradicting the warning at this boundary. Preserve that encoding and recheck final renderer on source changes.

proposedDismissal.comment: The destination is percent-encoded, including backslashes, before Markdown interpolation; the reported backslash bypass is addressed by the adjacent encoding.

mobile-markdown.justification: Mobile Markdown link conversion needs backslash/label/destination parsing verified end-to-end. Mobile is not distributed by this fork release, but the source finding is retained; no blanket mobile exclusion or dismissal.

qr-numeric-cells.justification: QR generator writes boolean array cells using private numeric coordinates from bounded version/mask loops. The reported assignment does not take an attacker-selected string property such as __proto__. Preserve Nayuki attribution and generator behavior.

proposedDismissal.comment: The reported key is a bounded numeric QR matrix coordinate generated by private loops, not an attacker-controlled property name; the assignment cannot select __proto__.

protocol-gated-links.justification: OpenMediaLink permits http/https/blob before href; PR attachment splitting permits http/https before rendering. These source protocol gates support the individual XSS dispositions. Remote-content policy is a separate boundary and remains enforced.

proposedDismissal.comment: The reported link receives a destination restricted to allowed non-script protocols by its source validation; it cannot become a javascript URL at this sink.

video-callers.justification: SARIF traces a protocol-filtered PR attachment into video src, which is a media-fetch boundary. Inventory the other callers before final disposition. A proposed XSS false positive would not approve automatic remote content.

mobile-draft-id.justification: Math.random originates in a local new-task draft key; account identity appears to come from session input. Confirm all ID consumers are non-security-sensitive before proposing false positive. Mobile is not part of safe DMG/CLI distribution.

worker-method-dispatch.justification: Office worker dispatch looks up a user-selected property on a plain handler object, accepting inherited Object methods. Dedicated worker callers are local Office components; broader security impact is unproved. Restrict dispatch to own handler keys with protocol-level regressions. Main CodeQL must reanalyze after merge.

localRemediation.validation: Three inherited-property cases fail before the patch; all five protocol cases pass after Object.hasOwn enforcement. Fresh main CodeQL analysis remains pending.
localRemediation.mainVerification: pending human merge and fresh main audit/analysis

new-hono-audit-findings.justification: Fresh 2026-11-13 all-severity audit reports seven additional Hono/@hono/node-server advisories through apps/server > @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk > @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Dependency paths are verified by the audit; input-to-sink reachability and compatible remediation are not reviewed. These findings are outside the original parser/forge patch batch and remain unresolved, with no risk acceptance. The current audit contains nine advisory records including the existing Zod 3 and deepmerge residuals.
